 Nebraska fires Dana Holgorsen, promotes Glenn Thomas to OC
 Robin Washut @ RobinWashut 31m 0 Share Share 
 Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule made a significant midseason change Saturday, relieving offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties and handing play-calling responsibilities to co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas .
 In a statement released by the program, Rhule acknowledged the frustration with the Huskers’ results this season and took full responsibility for the program’s direction.
 “Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed, and I am frustrated with our results this season,” Rhule said. “As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program—including wins and losses—and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted.”
 Rhule cited the offense as the primary concern.
 “While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution are simply not working,” he said. “Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties.”
 Rhule praised Holgorsen’s knowledge and contributions in Lincoln but said the current results necessitated a different approach. Thomas, who has served as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, will now handle play-calling for the rest of the season.
 The move comes amid a difficult stretch for the Huskers, who have dropped four straight games after a 5-0 start. Offensive inconsistency has been a recurring issue during that slide, and Rhule said he will keep evaluating the program through the rest of the season and after it ends.
 “I will continue to evaluate our program through the season and certainly at its conclusion and make additional changes where I believe they will help us win,” Rhule said.
 He also addressed the fan base directly, recognizing the high expectations in Lincoln while asking for continued support of the players with several games remaining.
 “The Nebraska fan base has high expectations, and I embrace them, and I also know of their passionate support of the young men in our program,” Rhule said. “I hope they will continue to be there for our players with very important games still ahead. Our entire program is determined to finish this season strong.”
 Thomas now inherits an offense that has struggled to find consistency and identity in recent weeks. How quickly he can make an impact in the remaining schedule will be a key storyline as Nebraska tries to salvage its season.
